rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation removes __syncthreads() from instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine version). However, ModelNew creates InstanceNorm2dCustom with default affine=True, which means weight and bias are defined nn.Parameters. In instance_norm_forward_cuda, the condition `weight.defined() && bias.defined()` is TRUE, so it always calls instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, never the mutated instance_norm_forward_kernel.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation is in dead code within this fixed configuration. The model class InstanceNorm2dCustom has affine=True by default, creating nn.Parameter weight and bias tensors. When forward() is called, these defined parameters are passed to the CUDA function, which checks `if (weight.defined() && bias.defined())`. Since this condition is always true, the code always dispatches to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, which has the __syncthreads() intact. The mutated instance_norm_forward_kernel function is never invoked.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The mutated kernel can only be triggered if affine=False was passed to InstanceNorm2dCustom, but the model configuration is fixed with affine=True. No value-level input can change which kernel is called.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing CUDA kernels, ensure mutations target code paths that are actually reachable under the test configuration. Consider adding test configurations that exercise both affine and non-affine paths, or implement the mutation in both kernel variants to ensure coverage.
